definitions.explanation: February 14th, a day for expressing romantic feelings, observed in Japan primarily by women giving chocolate to men

examples.japanese: バレンタインデー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧チョコ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I received chocolate on Valentine's Day.

examples.japanese: バレンタインデー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧チョコ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧だ。
examples.english: I plan to give handmade chocolate on Valentine's Day.

examples.japanese: バレンタインデー⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{近|ちか}づく→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦デパート→デパート：01022_depaato⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{特設|とくせつ}⟦コーナー→コーナー：10865_koonaa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦チョコレート→チョコレート：05183_chokoreeto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: As Valentine's Day approaches, chocolates line the special displays at department stores.

notes:
A loanword from English. In Japan, Valentine's Day has a distinctive custom: women give chocolate to men, not the other way around. Men reciprocate one month later on ⟦ホワイトデー→ホワイトデー：25279_howaitodee⟧ (March 14th).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- バレンタインデー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧チョコ: Valentine's Day chocolate
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧チョコ: obligation chocolate (given to male coworkers, friends)
- {本命|ほんめい}チョコ: true-feelings chocolate (given to a romantic interest)
- ⟦{友|とも}→友：03466_tomo⟧チョコ: friend chocolate (exchanged between female friends)
- ⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧チョコ: handmade chocolate

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Japanese chocolate industry heavily promoted Valentine's Day starting in the 1950s-60s, establishing the tradition of women giving chocolate. The types of chocolate given carry social significance: {本命|ほんめい}チョコ indicates genuine romantic interest, while ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧チョコ is a social obligation in workplaces. In recent years, ⟦{友|とも}→友：03466_tomo⟧チョコ (exchanging chocolate among friends) has become popular among younger women.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦ホワイトデー→ホワイトデー：25279_howaitodee⟧: White Day (March 14th) — when men give return gifts
